concepts.title: ฐานข้อมูลเชิงสัมพันธ์และ SELECT แรกใน SQLite
concepts.covers: From zero: what a database/DBMS/relational database is (table = entity, row = record, column = attribute, Primary Key, Foreign Key, schema) using the shop ER diagram; SQL as a declarative language (say WHAT, not HOW); SQL statement anatomy (keywords in UPPERCASE by convention, semicolon, -- comments); sqlite3 CLI basics (.tables, .schema products, .headers on, .mode box, .quit) and ~/.sqliterc from Part 1. SELECT column list vs SELECT *, computed expressions (price * stock), column alias with AS, ORDER BY (ASC/DESC, multiple keys), LIMIT and OFFSET. Example file notes/c01_select.sql run with `sqlite3 shop.db < notes/c01_select.sql`: (1) `.tables`, (2) all active products name/price/stock ordered by price DESC, (3) stock_value = price * stock aliased, ORDER BY stock_value DESC LIMIT 5, (4) customers ordered by joined_on with LIMIT 3 OFFSET 3 (page 2). Show real box-mode output. Mistakes with real SQLite messages: `Parse error: no such column: prise`, `Parse error: no such table: product`, `Parse error: near "FROM": syntax error` (trailing comma before FROM), forgetting the semicolon in interactive mode (prompt changes to `   ...>`).

concepts.title: กรองข้อมูลด้วย WHERE, ตัวดำเนินการ, NULL, COALESCE และ CASE
concepts.covers: WHERE with = <> < > <= >=, AND/OR/NOT and parentheses precedence, IN, BETWEEN (inclusive), LIKE with % and _ (SQLite LIKE is case-insensitive for ASCII; PostgreSQL LIKE is case-sensitive and has ILIKE — preview), DISTINCT; NULL semantics: three-valued logic, why `city = NULL` returns nothing, IS NULL / IS NOT NULL, NULL in ORDER BY (SQLite puts NULL first in ASC), COALESCE(city, 'ไม่ระบุ'); simple and searched CASE expressions to label rows (price bands: 'ราคาประหยัด' < 1000, 'ราคากลาง' 1000–9999, 'ราคาสูง' >= 10000). Example file notes/c02_where_null.sql: products priced BETWEEN 500 AND 3000 AND stock > 0 ordered by price DESC; customers WHERE city IN ('Bangkok','Phuket') OR city IS NULL; names LIKE '%Phone%' / 'S%'; SELECT DISTINCT city; `WHERE city = NULL` (0 rows) vs `IS NULL` (Duangjai Saendee); COALESCE display; CASE price bands for active products. Mistakes: `= NULL` returning nothing silently, AND/OR precedence bug returning inactive products, `"Bangkok"` in double quotes treated as identifier (SQLite falls back to string with a warning in some builds; PostgreSQL errors `column "Bangkok" does not exist`), BETWEEN with reversed bounds giving 0 rows.

concepts.title: สร้างตารางด้วย Data Types และ Constraints
concepts.covers: Data types: SQLite storage classes (NULL, INTEGER, REAL, TEXT, BLOB) and type affinity, STRICT tables (SQLite 3.37+) vs PostgreSQL types (INTEGER, BIGINT, NUMERIC(10,2), TEXT, VARCHAR(n), BOOLEAN, DATE, TIMESTAMPTZ); why money should be NUMERIC not REAL (0.1+0.2); constraints PRIMARY KEY, FOREIGN KEY ... REFERENCES with ON DELETE CASCADE / RESTRICT, UNIQUE (single and composite), NOT NULL, CHECK, DEFAULT (CURRENT_TIMESTAMP); PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON is required in SQLite; DROP TABLE IF EXISTS; ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN. Example file notes/c03_reviews.sql creating table `reviews` (review_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, product_id FK -> products ON DELETE CASCADE, customer_id FK -> customers, rating INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (rating BETWEEN 1 AND 5), comment TEXT, created_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, UNIQUE (product_id, customer_id)) as a STRICT table, inserting 3 valid reviews (Somchai rates Laptop Pro 14 = 5, Somying rates SQL for Beginners = 4, Wichai rates Smartphone X = 3), then one violating insert per constraint run via separate sqlite3 calls so each real error shows: `CHECK constraint failed: rating BETWEEN 1 AND 5`, `UNIQUE constraint failed: reviews.product_id, reviews.customer_id`, `FOREIGN KEY constraint failed`, `NOT NULL constraint failed: reviews.rating`, and STRICT `cannot store TEXT value in INTEGER column reviews.rating`. Show the PostgreSQL equivalent CREATE TABLE (GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY, TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT now()) as a second file for comparison (not run until c05). The reviews table is used again in later concepts and Part 3; drop it at the end with a reset note.

concepts.title: เพิ่ม แก้ไข ลบข้อมูล (INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE) และ Transaction เบื้องต้น
concepts.covers: INSERT single row and multi-row VALUES, naming columns explicitly, INSERT ... RETURNING (SQLite 3.35+ and PostgreSQL), last_insert_rowid(); UPDATE with WHERE and expressions (stock = stock - 1), the danger of UPDATE/DELETE without WHERE (test with SELECT first); DELETE and FK protection (deleting Somchai Jaidee fails: `FOREIGN KEY constraint failed`); BEGIN / COMMIT / ROLLBACK basics; INSERT OR IGNORE / ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING / upsert ON CONFLICT(email) DO UPDATE (works in SQLite 3.24+ and PostgreSQL); resetting shop.db with `rm shop.db && sqlite3 shop.db < shop_schema_sqlite.sql && sqlite3 shop.db < shop_seed.sql`. Example file notes/c04_dml.sql: inside BEGIN...COMMIT add customer 'Kanya Srisuk' (kanya@example.com, Chiang Mai, 2026-07-01) with RETURNING customer_id (9), add order 15 for her dated 2026-07-02 status 'paid' with 2 items (Wireless Mouse x2 @590, Phone Case x1 @290), UPDATE stock for those products and show before/after; then a BEGIN; DELETE FROM order_items; SELECT COUNT(*) (0); ROLLBACK; SELECT COUNT(*) (back to 24) demo; then upsert changing Kanya's city. Tell learners to reset shop.db after this concept so later outputs match the original seed. Mistakes: `UNIQUE constraint failed: customers.email`, `FOREIGN KEY constraint failed` on delete, `cannot commit - no transaction is active`, `table customers has 5 columns but 4 values were supplied`.

concepts.title: สรุปข้อมูลด้วย Aggregate, GROUP BY, HAVING และฟังก์ชันข้อความกับวันที่ (SQLite เทียบ PostgreSQL)
concepts.covers: First concept that uses PostgreSQL 16 (database `shop` created in the setup section). Aggregates COUNT(*) vs COUNT(city) (8 vs 7) vs COUNT(DISTINCT city), SUM, AVG, MIN, MAX; GROUP BY one and several columns; every non-aggregated column must be in GROUP BY (PostgreSQL error `column "products.name" must appear in the GROUP BY clause or be used in an aggregate function`, SQLite silently allows it — explain why that is dangerous); WHERE vs HAVING and logical query order (FROM, WHERE, GROUP BY, HAVING, SELECT, ORDER BY, LIMIT); conditional aggregation with SUM(CASE ...) and PostgreSQL FILTER (WHERE ...); integer division trap (7/2 = 3) and fixes (* 1.0, ::numeric, ROUND(x, 2)); string functions: || concatenation, UPPER, LOWER, LENGTH, SUBSTR, REPLACE, TRIM, split_part (PG only); date functions: SQLite strftime('%Y-%m', order_date), date('now'), julianday vs PostgreSQL date_trunc('month', order_date), to_char(order_date, 'YYYY-MM'), EXTRACT, CURRENT_DATE, age(), interval arithmetic order_date + INTERVAL '7 days'. Example: same monthly sales report (excluding cancelled) written twice — notes/c05_monthly_sqlite.sql (run with sqlite3) and notes/c05_monthly_pg.sql (run with `psql -d shop -f`), showing the 6 months 2026-01 40570, 2026-02 21120, 2026-03 57380, 2026-04 17120, 2026-05 3950, 2026-06 19870 (PG shows NUMERIC 40570.00), plus HAVING revenue > 20000 and a status breakdown with FILTER; then a short string/date query on customers (UPPER(name), split_part email domain, joined month, days since joining relative to the fixed date DATE '2026-10-20' so output is reproducible). Comparison table SQLite vs PostgreSQL for each function used.

concepts.title: เชื่อมตารางด้วย JOIN ทุกแบบและ Set Operations
concepts.covers: Run on PostgreSQL 16 (note: SQLite 3.39+ also supports RIGHT and FULL JOIN, so 3.45.1 runs them too). Text diagrams (Venn-style and row-matching) for INNER, LEFT, RIGHT, FULL OUTER, CROSS JOIN; ON vs USING; table aliases; join of 5 tables (customers-orders-order_items-products-categories); self join on categories (child with parent name); anti join (LEFT JOIN ... WHERE o.order_id IS NULL) to find Anan Thongkham who never ordered and products never sold (USB-C Hub, Old MP3 Player); row-count prediction exercise (customers 8 x orders 14: INNER 14, LEFT 15, CROSS 112); the LEFT JOIN + WHERE on right table trap that turns it back into INNER (move condition to ON); set operations UNION vs UNION ALL, INTERSECT, EXCEPT with matching column counts/types (e.g. cities of customers who ordered in Q1 EXCEPT those in Q2). Example file notes/c06_joins.sql with the 5-table join for order 7, LEFT JOIN order counts per customer (Anan = 0), self join categories, anti join, CROSS JOIN count, UNION vs UNION ALL of cities. Mistakes: `column reference "customer_id" is ambiguous`, missing join condition producing a Cartesian product, `each UNION query must have the same number of columns`, `missing FROM-clause entry for table "o"`.

concepts.title: Subquery และ CTE (WITH)
concepts.covers: PostgreSQL 16. Subquery kinds: scalar subquery in WHERE and SELECT (products priced above the average active price), IN subquery, EXISTS / NOT EXISTS, correlated subquery (latest order_date per customer, product with its category's max price), derived table in FROM (subquery with alias); the NOT IN + NULL trap demonstrated with a subquery that returns a NULL (returns 0 rows) and the fix with NOT EXISTS; three ways to find never-sold products (NOT IN, NOT EXISTS, LEFT JOIN anti join) giving the same 2 rows; CTE with WITH, multiple CTEs chained (order_totals -> customer_totals -> customers above average spend), CTE vs subquery readability, CTEs are not materialized by default in PG 12+ (MATERIALIZED / NOT MATERIALIZED hint). Example file notes/c07_subquery_cte.sql. Mistakes: `more than one row returned by a subquery used as an expression`, `subquery in FROM must have an alias` (note: PG 16 no longer requires the alias — verify; writer must run and show what 16 actually does), `relation "order_totals" does not exist` when using a CTE name outside its statement, NOT IN with NULL returning nothing.

concepts.title: ออกแบบฐานข้อมูล: Normalization 1NF–3NF, Denormalization และ View
concepts.covers: PostgreSQL 16. Data modeling workflow: entities, attributes, relationships (1:1, 1:N, M:N via junction table), cardinality, ER diagram in text and in Mermaid erDiagram for README; anomalies (insert, update, delete) shown on a flat table `orders_flat` (order_id, order_date, customer_name, customer_email, customer_city, product_names as comma list 'Laptop Pro 14, Wireless Mouse', category_name, unit_price, quantity); 1NF (atomic values, no repeating groups), 2NF (no partial dependency on part of a composite key), 3NF (no transitive dependency: customer_city depends on customer_email); normalizing the flat table step by step with CREATE TABLE ... and INSERT ... SELECT DISTINCT inside a schema `lab` (CREATE SCHEMA lab) so the main shop tables stay untouched; why order_items.unit_price is a deliberate historical snapshot, not redundancy; denormalization trade-offs (read speed vs write anomalies, reporting tables); CREATE VIEW v_order_summary (order_id, customer name, order_date, status, total) and querying it, CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW, MATERIALIZED VIEW mv_monthly_sales + REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW and showing stale data before refresh, DROP VIEW. Example files notes/c08_normalize.sql and notes/c08_views.sql with real psql output. Mistakes: `cannot drop table orders because other objects depend on it` (view dependency, HINT: Use DROP ... CASCADE), `cannot change name of view column`, stale materialized view, update anomaly example.

concepts.title: Window Functions และ Recursive CTE
concepts.covers: PostgreSQL 16 (SQLite 3.25+ also supports window functions; mention). GROUP BY collapses rows vs OVER keeps rows; OVER (), PARTITION BY, ORDER BY in the window, frame clause ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW vs the default RANGE frame; ROW_NUMBER vs RANK vs DENSE_RANK on ties (products ranked by price within category; Smartphone X and Laptop Pro 14 etc.; add a tie example using unit sales quantity where ties exist); SUM() OVER (ORDER BY month) running total; AVG() moving average of 3 months; LAG/LEAD for month-over-month growth with NULLIF to avoid division by zero; NTILE(4); Top-N per group with a CTE + ROW_NUMBER() and WHERE rn <= 2 (best-selling products per top-level category); share of total with SUM() OVER (); WINDOW clause naming. Recursive CTE: WITH RECURSIVE anchor + recursive member + termination, category tree with depth and path 'Electronics > Computers > Computer Accessories', generating a calendar of months with generate_series vs recursive CTE, cycle protection (depth < 10 / CYCLE clause in PG 14+). Example files notes/c09_window.sql (monthly revenue, running_total, prev_month, growth_pct; ranking) and notes/c09_recursive.sql. Mistakes: `window functions are not allowed in WHERE` (wrap in CTE), forgetting ORDER BY in OVER making running total equal grand total, `recursive query "tree" column 3 has type character varying ... in non-recursive term but type text overall` style type mismatch (fix with ::text), infinite recursion.

concepts.title: Index, EXPLAIN และ EXPLAIN ANALYZE
concepts.covers: How a B-tree index works (phone-book analogy), sequential scan vs index scan vs bitmap heap scan vs index only scan; creating a big practice table in PostgreSQL with generate_series: `big_orders` 200,000 rows with deterministic values (customer_id = (g % 5000) + 1, order_date = DATE '2025-01-01' + (g % 540), amount = ((g * 37) % 100000) / 100.0, status from an array by g % 4) so every reader gets identical data; ANALYZE; EXPLAIN vs EXPLAIN ANALYZE (actually runs the query — careful with UPDATE/DELETE, wrap in BEGIN/ROLLBACK) and EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS); reading cost=, rows=, actual time=, loops=, Rows Removed by Filter; \timing in psql; CREATE INDEX on customer_id, composite index (customer_id, order_date) and the leftmost-prefix rule, partial index WHERE status = 'pending', expression index on lower(email), UNIQUE index, CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY for production; why LIKE '%x' and functions on columns cannot use a plain B-tree; costs of indexes (write overhead, disk size via pg_relation_size / \di+), when the planner prefers seq scan (small tables, low selectivity); SQLite EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN on shop.db (`SCAN orders` vs `SEARCH orders USING INDEX idx_orders_customer (customer_id=?)`) and .timer on. Example files notes/c10_index_pg.sql and notes/c10_index_sqlite.sql. Timing numbers differ per machine — say so and show the sandbox run; plan shapes must be real. Mistakes: index not used because of type mismatch or function on column, forgetting ANALYZE after bulk load, `relation "idx_big_orders_customer" already exists` (use IF NOT EXISTS), running EXPLAIN ANALYZE on DELETE and losing data.

concepts.title: Transaction, ACID, Isolation Level, Lock และ Backup/Restore
concepts.covers: PostgreSQL 16. ACID explained with selling one product (create order + add item + decrement stock); BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK, SAVEPOINT / ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT; PostgreSQL aborted-transaction state `ERROR:  current transaction is aborted, commands ignored until end of transaction block`; concurrency anomalies (dirty read, non-repeatable read, phantom read, lost update, write skew); isolation levels READ COMMITTED (default), REPEATABLE READ, SERIALIZABLE (READ UNCOMMITTED behaves as READ COMMITTED); TWO-SESSION DEMO: show Session A and Session B side by side as numbered timeline steps (t1, t2, ...) in a table plus each session's real psql output, reading Wireless Mouse stock (60) while the other session updates it to 59 and commits — READ COMMITTED sees 59 in the second read, REPEATABLE READ still sees 60, and a concurrent UPDATE under REPEATABLE READ fails with `ERROR:  could not serialize access due to concurrent update` (app must retry); the writer produces real outputs by driving two psql sessions in the sandbox (e.g. two background psql processes fed via named pipes, or psycopg two connections) but presents them to the learner as two terminal windows; SELECT ... FOR UPDATE to prevent overselling and lock wait behaviour; `deadlock detected` explanation; keep transactions short. Backup/restore as Durability safety net: pg_dump plain SQL (-f backups/shop.sql) and custom format (-Fc), pg_restore into shop_restore, psql -f restore of the plain dump, verify row counts, pg_dumpall --globals-only for roles, SQLite `.backup backups/shop_copy.db` and `.dump`; mention cron from topic 19 for scheduled backups. Code shown as wsl blocks (psql sessions) plus file blocks for SQL.

concepts.title: ใช้ SQL จาก Python: sqlite3, psycopg 3, SQL Injection และ Role สิทธิ์น้อยที่สุด
concepts.covers: Python 3.12 inside ~/projects/sql-lab/.venv with psycopg[binary]==3.3.6. sqlite3 module: connect, execute, fetchone/fetchall, executemany, row_factory = sqlite3.Row, ? and :name placeholders, `with conn:` commits/rolls back but does not close (use contextlib.closing or conn.close()); SQL injection recap with find_customer.py from Part 1 (x' OR '1'='1 -> 8 rows vs 0); psycopg 3: psycopg.connect(os.environ.get('DATABASE_URL', 'postgresql:///shop')) via Unix socket + peer auth, %s and %(name)s placeholders (NOT Python % formatting), row_factory=dict_row, cur.executemany, conn.transaction() blocks, `with psycopg.connect() as conn` commits on success / rolls back on exception / closes; catching psycopg.errors.UniqueViolation and CheckViolation; dynamic identifiers with psycopg.sql.SQL / sql.Identifier and an allowlist for ORDER BY columns; least-privilege roles: SQL file notes/c12_roles.sql creating role shop_app LOGIN PASSWORD from a psql variable (never hard-coded in git; the example uses \password or reads it with `\prompt`), GRANT CONNECT ON DATABASE, GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA public, GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE ON orders/order_items, SELECT on products/customers, GRANT USAGE on identity sequences is not needed for GENERATED ALWAYS identity (verify and state what is actually needed), REVOKE, ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES, \du and \dp, proving `ERROR:  permission denied for table customers` on DELETE; and a read-only role report_reader. Main runnable example file place_order.py: function place_order(conn, customer_email, items) that, in ONE transaction, looks up the customer, locks product rows with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE, checks stock, inserts the order with RETURNING order_id, inserts order_items with executemany, decrements stock, and raises a custom OutOfStock error that rolls everything back; the script runs one successful order and one failing order (USB-C Hub stock 0) and prints stock before/after to prove atomicity. Mistakes: `psycopg.OperationalError: connection failed: ... role "somchai" does not exist`, `psycopg.errors.UndefinedTable`, `TypeError: not all arguments converted during string formatting`/`the query has 1 placeholders but 0 parameters were passed`, passing a single value instead of a tuple ((x,) not (x)), forgetting commit in sqlite3 so data is not saved, `sqlite3.ProgrammingError: Incorrect number of bindings supplied`.

mini_project.name: E-commerce Database
mini_project.summary: Design and build a production-style e-commerce database in PostgreSQL 16 as a portfolio repository named ecommerce-db at ~/projects/ecommerce-db: 6 tables (customers, categories, products, orders, order_items, payments) with full constraints and indexes, a deterministic seed script (no random()), an ER diagram in text (ASCII + Mermaid in README), 20 analytical queries answering business questions with their real outputs saved to results/, EXPLAIN ANALYZE-based index tuning documented before/after, and a Python report script using psycopg 3 parameterized queries. Everything is rebuilt from scratch with one command (make-style shell script).
features: Folder layout: ~/projects/ecommerce-db/ with README.md, .gitignore (.venv/, results/*.tmp, .env), requirements.txt (psycopg[binary]==3.3.6), schema/01_tables.sql, schema/02_indexes.sql, seed/seed.sql, queries/q01_*.sql ... queries/q20_*.sql, results/q01.txt ... results/q20.txt, docs/er.md, docs/explain.md, scripts/rebuild.sh, scripts/run_queries.sh, report.py

Database name ecommerce (separate from the practice database shop); created with createdb ecommerce; scripts/rebuild.sh runs dropdb --if-exists ecommerce, createdb ecommerce, then psql -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -q for schema, seed, and indexes

Schema: customers (customer_id IDENTITY PK, full_name, email UNIQUE NOT NULL, phone, province, created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT now()), categories (category_id IDENTITY PK, name UNIQUE, parent_id self FK), products (product_id IDENTITY PK, sku UNIQUE, name, category_id FK, price NUMERIC(10,2) CHECK >= 0, stock INTEGER CHECK >= 0, is_active BOOLEAN DEFAULT TRUE), orders (order_id IDENTITY PK, customer_id FK, ordered_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL, status TEXT CHECK IN ('pending','paid','shipped','delivered','cancelled'), shipping_fee NUMERIC(10,2) DEFAULT 0), order_items (order_id FK ON DELETE CASCADE, product_id FK, quantity CHECK > 0, unit_price NUMERIC(10,2), PRIMARY KEY (order_id, product_id)), payments (payment_id IDENTITY PK, order_id FK UNIQUE, method TEXT CHECK IN ('credit_card','promptpay','bank_transfer','cod'), amount NUMERIC(10,2) CHECK > 0, paid_at TIMESTAMPTZ, status CHECK IN ('success','failed','refunded'))

Deterministic seed: hand-written rows for categories (about 10 with 2 levels) and products (about 30 with SKUs), then generate_series with modular arithmetic for 500 customers, 5,000 orders across 2025-01-01 to 2026-06-30, about 12,000 order_items and payments for paid/shipped/delivered orders, so every learner gets identical query results; province values from a fixed array (Bangkok, Chiang Mai, Khon Kaen, Phuket, Chon Buri, Songkhla, Nakhon Ratchasima, Udon Thani) indexed by id % 8

20 analytical queries, each file starts with a Thai comment stating the business question: monthly revenue, revenue by category (recursive to top-level), top 10 products, top customers by lifetime value, average order value, orders per status, payment method share, repeat-customer rate, customers with no orders in the last 90 days relative to fixed date 2026-06-30, month-over-month growth with LAG, running total, Top-3 products per category with ROW_NUMBER, RFM-style segmentation with NTILE, cohort by first-order month, basket size distribution, products never sold, low-stock alert, cancelled-order rate by province, refund amount by month, day-of-week sales pattern
scripts/run_queries.sh runs every queries/*.sql with psql and writes results/qNN.txt; README embeds selected real outputs

Index tuning: docs/explain.md records EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) before and after adding indexes for at least 3 slow queries (orders(customer_id), orders(ordered_at), order_items(product_id), partial index on orders where status = 'pending'), with planning/execution time noted as machine-dependent

report.py: psycopg 3, connection string from DATABASE_URL env var (default postgresql:///ecommerce), argparse options --month YYYY-MM and --top N passed as %s parameters, dict_row, prints a formatted Thai monthly report (revenue, orders, AOV, top products) and optionally writes CSV with the csv module
Roles: ecommerce_report read-only role with GRANT SELECT, demonstrated permission denied on INSERT
Backup: pg_dump -Fc to backups/ecommerce.dump (backups/ in .gitignore) and a restore test into ecommerce_restore
README with Mermaid erDiagram, setup steps, how to rebuild, query list with business questions, sample outputs, and lessons learned; pushed to GitHub (topic 17)
mini_project.stack: Ubuntu 24.04 LTS (WSL2), PostgreSQL 16 (apt postgresql, psql 16), Python 3.12.3 + venv, psycopg[binary]==3.3.6, sqlfluff==4.4.0 (optional lint, dialect postgres), Git 2.43.0 + GitHub, Mermaid erDiagram rendered by GitHub

versions.sqlite3_cli: 3.45.1 (apt sqlite3); Python sqlite3 module also links 3.45.1
versions.postgresql: 16 (apt postgresql; Part 1 shows psql (PostgreSQL) 16.15 (Ubuntu 16.15-0ubuntu0.24.04.1)); latest upstream is 18, 19 is RC
versions.python: 3.12.3 system python3 (code must run on 3.12+); packages only inside ~/projects/sql-lab/.venv or ~/projects/ecommerce-db/.venv
versions.docker_desktop: 4.95.0 (optional, only for trying PostgreSQL 18 on port 5433)

notes: Learner username is somchai; home /home/somchai. Practice folder is ~/projects/sql-lab (git repo) with shop_schema_sqlite.sql, shop_schema_pg.sql, shop_seed.sql, shop.db, notes/, backups/, find_customer.py, .venv/. Mini Project folder is ~/projects/ecommerce-db.

Sample schema used everywhere (the 'shop'): customers(customer_id, name, email UNIQUE, city NULLable, joined_on), categories(category_id, name UNIQUE, parent_id self-FK), products(product_id, name, category_id, price, stock, is_active), orders(order_id, customer_id, order_date, status IN pending/paid/shipped/cancelled), order_items(order_id, product_id, quantity, unit_price, PK(order_id, product_id)). The exact schema and seed files are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/fe474bf2-4538-5703-885b-2ffd0c503494/scratchpad/work/t14/sql-lab/ (shop_schema_sqlite.sql, shop_schema_pg.sql, shop_seed.sql) — copy them verbatim; Part 2 setup must print the FULL contents of all three files so the page is self-contained. Do not change any seed value.

SQLite schema uses INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, REAL money, TEXT dates 'YYYY-MM-DD', is_active INTEGER 1/0 (seed writes TRUE/FALSE which SQLite stores as 1/0). PostgreSQL schema uses INTEGER GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY, NUMERIC(10,2), DATE, BOOLEAN. Seed inserts never specify ids, so ids are 1..n in insert order.

Seed facts to rely on: 8 customers (1 Somchai Jaidee Bangkok, 2 Somying Rakrian Chiang Mai, 3 Wichai Mankhong Khon Kaen, 4 Manee Meesuk Bangkok, 5 Piti Yindee Phuket, 6 Chujai Faidee Chiang Mai, 7 Duangjai Saendee city NULL, 8 Anan Thongkham Khon Kaen — never ordered); 7 categories (1 Electronics, 2 Computers<1, 3 Computer Accessories<2, 4 Mobile Phones<1, 5 Books, 6 Programming Books<5, 7 Home Appliances — no products); 10 products (1 Laptop Pro 14 35900, 2 27-inch Monitor 7990, 3 Mechanical Keyboard 2490, 4 Wireless Mouse 590 stock 60, 5 USB-C Hub 1290 stock 0 never sold, 6 Smartphone X 18990, 7 Phone Case 290, 8 SQL for Beginners 450, 9 Python Crash Course 690, 10 Old MP3 Player 990 inactive never sold); 14 orders 2026-01-05..2026-06-20 (order 5 cancelled; statuses shipped/paid/pending); 22 order_items. Revenue excluding cancelled = 160010; monthly: 2026-01 40570, 02 21120, 03 57380, 04 17120, 05 3950, 06 19870.

SQLite runs: `sqlite3 shop.db < notes/<file>.sql` with ~/.sqliterc (.headers on, .mode box, .nullvalue NULL, PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON) so output is box-drawing tables. In the sandbox create the same ~/.sqliterc before running so outputs match. PostgreSQL runs: `psql -d shop -f notes/<file>.sql` with ~/.psqlrc containing \pset null NULL (aligned format). Database names: shop (practice), shop_restore (restore test), ecommerce (Mini Project).

Concepts c01–c04 use SQLite only; from c05 on use PostgreSQL 16 as the main engine and point out SQLite differences. The Part 2 setup section installs sqlite3 AND postgresql, starts the service (sudo service postgresql start — WSL has no systemd by default in older setups; also mention systemctl if systemd is enabled), creates role somchai with sudo -u postgres createuser --createdb "$USER", createdb shop, and loads schema+seed exactly as Part 1 Step 7.

Any concept that modifies data (c03 reviews, c04 DML, c08 lab schema, c11 transactions, c12 place_order) must end with a reset/cleanup instruction so the next concept's outputs match the original seed: SQLite reset `rm -f shop.db && sqlite3 shop.db < shop_schema_sqlite.sql && sqlite3 shop.db < shop_seed.sql`; PostgreSQL reset `dropdb shop && createdb shop && psql -d shop -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -q -f shop_schema_pg.sql -f shop_seed.sql`.

When a query depends on 'today', use the fixed date DATE '2026-10-20' (or '2026-06-30' in the Mini Project) instead of CURRENT_DATE so outputs are reproducible; if CURRENT_DATE is shown, say the learner's value will differ.

SQL file naming: notes/cNN_<topic>.sql for Part 2 concepts, notes/ex_<n>.sql for Part 3 exercises. SQL keywords UPPERCASE, identifiers snake_case lowercase, Thai comments with --. Code comments in Thai.

Terminology (keep in English): Table, Row, Column, Primary Key, Foreign Key, Constraint, Query, Schema, Index, Transaction, Isolation Level, View, Materialized View, CTE, Subquery, Window Function, JOIN, Aggregate, Placeholder, Parameterized Query, SQL Injection, Role. Use 'คำสั่งซื้อ' for order, 'สินค้า' for product, 'ลูกค้า' for customer, 'หมวดสินค้า' for category.

Error messages must be the real ones from SQLite 3.45.1 / PostgreSQL 16 (e.g. SQLite CLI prints `Runtime error near line N: ... (19)` or `Parse error near line N: ...`; PostgreSQL prints `psql:notes/file.sql:N: ERROR:  ...`). Run every query in the sandbox (apt-get install -y sqlite3; service postgresql start; create role somchai or run as postgres with output adjusted to owner somchai).

Safety: SQL Injection examples only against the learner's own shop.db / local PostgreSQL; cite พ.ร.บ.ว่าด้วยการกระทำความผิดเกี่ยวกับคอมพิวเตอร์. Never hard-code passwords; use DATABASE_URL env var, peer auth via Unix socket (postgresql:///shop), \password, or .env in .gitignore.

Certifications: no single required SQL certification; vendor certifications exist (Oracle, Microsoft, PostgreSQL vendors such as EDB) — tell learners to verify current names and exam codes on the vendor site; Microsoft PL-300 is active (data analyst, uses SQL indirectly).
Cross-topic links: Linux (WSL, apt, cron), Git and GitHub (push Mini Project), Python (venv, functions, exceptions), Prompt Engineering (asking AI to explain query plans, always verify).
